title: Cheapest Courier
statement: A courier company has n depots numbered 0 to n − 1 and one-way routes [from, to, cost]. Return the cheapest total cost to send a parcel from depot 0 to depot n − 1, or −1 if it cannot get there.

answerKey.pattern: Dijkstra's algorithm with a min-heap of (distance, depot)
keyPoints: Distances start at infinity except depot 0
Take the closest unsettled depot from the heap; skip stale entries
Relax each outgoing route: if dist[u] + cost < dist[v], update and push
edgeCases: Several routes between the same depots
The direct route is not the cheapest

hints: Why does BFS give the wrong answer here?
Costs differ, so the fewest routes is not the cheapest. Always expand the cheapest known depot next.
Use a min-heap; when you pop a depot with a distance larger than its best, skip it.
